sentences.text: Adratiklit boulahfa is the only species within this extinct group of stegosaurian dinosaurs.
Its unique skeletal features are diagnostic for the entire Stegosauria group.
This animal is considered one of the oldest known stegosaurs, alongside Thyreosaurus.
It holds the distinction of being the oldest definitive stegosaur found anywhere in the world.
Susannah Maidment and colleagues described the genus on August 16, 2019, based on a single dorsal vertebra cataloged as NHMUK PV R37366.
The Natural History Museum in the United Kingdom acquired these fossils from fossil traders.
Evidence suggests the remains represent multiple individuals, estimated to be around five, including a humerus measuring 61 centimeters in length.
Adratiklit is the first described eurypodan dinosaur taxon found in North Africa.
The genus belongs to the family Stegosauridae and is classified within the subfamily Dacentrurinae.
It is more closely related to European stegosaurs like Dacentrurus and Miragaia than to southern African taxa.
Adratiklit lived on the supercontinent Gondwana during the Middle Jurassic, specifically between 168.2 and 161.5 million years ago.
Remains were found in the El Mers Group near Boulahfa, south of Boulemane in Fès-Meknes, Morocco.
